options: these regions receive the highest rainfall on Earth, diluting the salt content
these regions are farthest from any river mouths
high rates of evaporation under stable high-pressure conditions remove fresh water, concentrating the remaining salt
polar ice constantly melts into these waters, increasing salinity
questions.explanation: Subtropical high-pressure zones experience high evaporation rates and relatively low rainfall, which removes fresh water from the ocean surface and leaves a higher concentration of dissolved salts.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: Spring tides, which produce the greatest tidal range, occur when
options: the moon is at its greatest distance from the Earth
there is no gravitational influence from the moon at all
the sun and moon are positioned at right angles relative to the Earth
the sun, Earth, and moon are roughly aligned, so the gravitational pulls of the sun and moon combine
questions.explanation: Spring tides occur during the new and full moon phases, when the sun, Earth, and moon are approximately aligned, causing the gravitational effects of the sun and moon to reinforce each other and produce the largest tidal range.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: The continental shelf is best described as the
options: gently sloping, submerged extension of a continent, extending from the coastline to the point where the ocean floor drops steeply into deep water
deepest part of the ocean floor, found in ocean trenches
narrow strip of exposed sand along a coastline
central ridge running along the middle of an ocean basin
questions.explanation: The continental shelf is the relatively shallow, gently sloping submerged margin of a continent, extending seaward from the coast until the seabed steepens sharply at the continental slope.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: Longshore drift is the process by which
options: rivers deposit sediment exclusively at their source
sediment is transported along a coastline in a zig-zag pattern, driven by waves approaching the shore at an angle
wind transports sand from coastal dunes far inland
ocean currents dissolve coastal rock chemically
questions.explanation: Longshore drift occurs when waves approach a beach at an angle, moving sediment up the beach at that angle (swash) and back down at right angles (backwash), gradually transporting material along the coast in a zig-zag path.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: Upwelling, a process that supports rich fishing grounds along certain coastlines such as off Peru and Namibia, occurs when
options: rivers deposit large amounts of sediment directly offshore
warm surface water sinks directly to the ocean floor
prevailing winds push surface water away from the coast, allowing cold, nutrient-rich water from deeper layers to rise and replace it
tidal action alone causes deep water to rise to the surface twice daily
questions.explanation: Upwelling occurs when winds drive surface water away from the coast, drawing cold, nutrient-rich water up from the depths to replace it, which boosts plankton growth and supports abundant fish populations.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: The Gulf Stream, a warm ocean current, has a significant moderating effect on the climate of
options: the eastern coast of South America
the eastern coast of Australia
the Sahara Desert region
north-western Europe, keeping winters milder than expected for its latitude
questions.explanation: The Gulf Stream carries warm water from the Gulf of Mexico across the Atlantic towards north-western Europe, significantly moderating winter temperatures there compared to other regions at similar latitudes.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: According to the demographic transition model, a country in the 'early expanding' stage is typically characterised by
options: high birth rates combined with rapidly falling death rates, resulting in rapid population growth
high birth rates and high death rates, resulting in slow population growth
low birth rates and low death rates, resulting in slow or stable population growth
low birth rates and high death rates, resulting in population decline
questions.explanation: In the early expanding stage of the demographic transition model, death rates fall sharply (due to improved healthcare and sanitation) while birth rates remain high, producing rapid population growth.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: The concept of 'optimum population' refers to a population size at which
options: a country experiences its highest possible birth rate
the available resources and level of technology allow for the maximum output per capita, given the existing population
a region has reached its maximum possible number of inhabitants without exception
there is complete absence of unemployment in every economic sector
questions.explanation: Optimum population describes the population size that, given the resources and technology available, yields the highest standard of living or output per person, distinct from either overpopulation or underpopulation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: A region is said to be 'overpopulated' when
options: its population density is higher than that of any neighbouring region, regardless of resources
the total population figure is greater than one million people
its population exceeds the level that the available resources and technology can adequately support, given the existing standard of living
the birth rate exceeds the death rate by any margin
questions.explanation: Overpopulation is a relative condition in which population size exceeds what the available resources, technology, and organisation can support at an adequate standard of living, rather than simply a high absolute number.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: A country records 50,000 immigrants and 30,000 emigrants in a given year. What is the net migration figure for that year?
options: Net migration of -20,000 (net emigration)
Net migration of 0 (balanced)
Net migration of +80,000
Net migration of +20,000 (net immigration)
questions.explanation: Net migration = immigrants - emigrants = 50,000 - 30,000 = +20,000, indicating a net inflow (net immigration) of 20,000 people.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: A 'primate city' in urban geography refers to a city that
options: is disproportionately larger and more dominant (economically, politically, and demographically) than any other city in its country
has the smallest population among a country's major cities
is located exclusively along a coastline
was the very first settlement ever established in a country
questions.explanation: A primate city is disproportionately larger than the second-largest city in its country and dominates national economic, political, and cultural life, unlike a more balanced urban hierarchy.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: In settlement geography, the distinction between a settlement's 'site' and its 'situation' is that
options: site and situation are simply two different words for the same concept
site refers to the immediate physical land the settlement occupies, while situation refers to its location relative to surrounding physical and human features
site refers only to a settlement's population size, while situation refers to its street layout
site refers to a settlement's economic function, while situation refers to its administrative status
questions.explanation: Site describes the actual physical land on which a settlement is built (e.g., a hill, a river confluence), while situation describes its position relative to surrounding features, such as neighbouring towns, transport routes, or resources.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: A rural settlement pattern in which dwellings develop radiating outward from a central point, often following roads that converge like spokes of a wheel, is best described as a
options: dispersed pattern
purely linear pattern
radial (or star-shaped) pattern
checkerboard grid pattern
questions.explanation: A radial settlement pattern develops where roads converge on a central point (such as a market or road junction), with buildings extending outward along each route, forming a star-like shape distinct from a simple nucleated cluster.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: A region has a total population of 2,000,000 people and a total land area of 40,000 square kilometres. What is the population density of the region?
options: 20 persons per square kilometre
500 persons per square kilometre
80 persons per square kilometre
50 persons per square kilometre
questions.explanation: Population density = total population / total land area = 2,000,000 / 40,000 = 50 persons per square kilometre.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: Iron and steel manufacturing has traditionally been described as a 'bulk-reducing' (raw-material-oriented) industry mainly because
options: the raw materials (iron ore and coal) are heavy and lose considerable weight during processing, so factories locate near the raw material source to minimise transport costs
the finished product weighs significantly more than the raw materials used to produce it
the industry requires no raw materials at all
the finished steel products are always sold in the same location where they are produced
questions.explanation: Because iron ore and coal are heavy and much of their bulk is lost as waste during smelting, it is cheaper to locate iron and steel plants near the raw material sources rather than transport the heavier raw inputs long distances.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: When a region concentrates its agricultural production on the crops or livestock best suited to its particular soil, climate, and resources, and trades for other goods, this practice reflects the economic principle of
options: subsistence farming exclusively
specialisation based on comparative advantage
shifting cultivation
transhumance
questions.explanation: Specialisation according to comparative advantage occurs when a region focuses production on the goods it can produce most efficiently given its natural conditions, then trades for other needs, rather than attempting to produce everything itself.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: Shifting cultivation (bush fallowing), traditionally practised in parts of tropical Africa, is characterised by
options: permanent cultivation of the same plot of land using heavy chemical fertiliser input
large-scale mechanised cultivation of a single cash crop for export
clearing and cultivating a plot of land for a few years, then abandoning it to restore soil fertility naturally while farming is shifted to a new plot
cultivation exclusively on irrigated land in arid regions
questions.explanation: Shifting cultivation involves farming a cleared plot for a limited period, then leaving it fallow to regain fertility naturally while cultivation moves to a newly cleared plot, a practice suited to fragile tropical soils.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: Which of the following best distinguishes plantation agriculture from subsistence farming?
options: Plantation agriculture is typically small-scale and focused on producing food only for the farmer's own family, while subsistence farming is large-scale and export-oriented
Plantation agriculture never involves any form of hired labour
Plantation agriculture and subsistence farming are simply different names for the same practice

Plantation agriculture is typically large-scale, often foreign-owned or corporate, and focused on producing a single cash crop for export, while subsistence farming is small-scale and aimed mainly at meeting the farmer's own household needs
questions.explanation: Plantation agriculture is generally large-scale, capital-intensive, and organised around producing a single cash crop for commercial export, in clear contrast to subsistence farming, which is small-scale and primarily geared towards meeting a household's own food needs.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: Transhumance refers to the practice by which
options: pastoralists move their livestock seasonally between highland (upland) summer pastures and lowland (valley) winter pastures
farmers cultivate the same crop on the same plot of land every year without interruption
fishing communities relocate permanently to coastal cities
manufacturers relocate factories to reduce transport costs
questions.explanation: Transhumance is the seasonal movement of livestock and herders between distinct pasture areas, typically higher altitude pastures in summer and lower, sheltered valleys in winter, to make the best use of available grazing throughout the year.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: A soft-drink bottling plant is typically described as a 'bulk-gaining' (market-oriented) industry because
options: its raw materials are far heavier than the finished product
the finished product (bottled drinks, including water added) is heavier and bulkier than its raw material inputs, so it is cheaper to locate the plant near the market it serves
it requires no transportation of any kind
it must always be located directly at the source of its raw materials, regardless of market location
questions.explanation: Since water is added during bottling, the finished product becomes heavier and bulkier than the concentrated raw inputs, making it more cost-effective to locate bottling plants close to the consumer market rather than the raw material source.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: A 'break-of-bulk point', such as a seaport, is significant in transport geography because it is a location where
options: goods must always be destroyed before being reloaded onto another form of transport
all agricultural production for a country is concentrated
goods are transferred from one mode of transport to another (for example, from ship to rail or road), often making it economically attractive for related industries to locate nearby
population density is always at its lowest
questions.explanation: A break-of-bulk point is where goods are transferred between different modes of transport (e.g., ship to rail), and the resulting cost and time savings often attract processing industries to locate at or near this point.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: Tourism is generally classified within which sector(s) of the economy?
options: Exclusively the primary sector, since it depends on natural resources
Exclusively the secondary sector, since it involves manufacturing
Exclusively the quaternary sector, since it involves scientific research alone
The tertiary and quaternary sectors, since it involves the provision of services, information, and experiences rather than the production of physical goods
questions.explanation: Tourism is generally categorised within the tertiary (and increasingly quaternary) sector, since it centres on providing services, hospitality, information, and experiences rather than extracting raw materials or manufacturing goods.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: For transporting large volumes of crude oil over long overland distances, a pipeline is generally preferred over rail transport mainly because
options: pipelines can move a continuous, high volume of liquid at relatively low operating cost once built, without the need for repeated loading and unloading
pipelines require significantly more labour to operate than rail networks
pipelines are cheaper to construct than any other mode of transport
rail transport cannot physically carry any liquid cargo at all
questions.explanation: Once constructed, pipelines offer a continuous, low-cost means of moving large volumes of liquid such as crude oil, without the repeated handling, loading, and unloading required by rail transport.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: The tendency of similar or related industries to cluster together in the same location, benefiting from shared infrastructure, suppliers, and a skilled labour pool, is known as
options: comparative disadvantage
agglomeration economies
subsistence clustering
transhumance
questions.explanation: Agglomeration economies describe the cost savings and other benefits that firms gain by locating near related industries, sharing infrastructure, specialised suppliers, and a pool of skilled labour.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: Moving from the coast towards the far north, Nigeria's natural vegetation belts occur in which general order?
options: Sahel savanna, Sudan savanna, Guinea savanna, tropical rainforest, mangrove swamp
Tropical rainforest, mangrove swamp, Sahel savanna, Sudan savanna, Guinea savanna
Mangrove swamp, tropical rainforest, Guinea savanna, Sudan savanna, Sahel savanna
Guinea savanna, mangrove swamp, tropical rainforest, Sudan savanna, Sahel savanna
questions.explanation: Nigeria's vegetation transitions from coastal mangrove swamp, through tropical rainforest, into Guinea savanna, then Sudan savanna, and finally the drier Sahel savanna in the far north, reflecting the general decline in rainfall from south to north.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: Nigeria's major drainage system, formed by the Niger and Benue rivers, ultimately empties into the Atlantic Ocean through
options: a single narrow river mouth with no distributaries
an underground aquifer system
an inland lake with no outlet to the sea
the Niger Delta, a large area of distributary channels and swamps in the south
questions.explanation: After converging at Lokoja, the combined Niger-Benue river system flows south and fans out into numerous distributary channels across the Niger Delta before discharging into the Atlantic Ocean.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: The Sahara, the world's largest hot desert, stretches across much of North Africa and is primarily characterised by
options: extremely low and unreliable rainfall, sparse vegetation, and a very wide daily temperature range
consistently high annual rainfall supporting dense forest
permanent snow and ice cover throughout the year
dense population settlement supported by abundant surface water
questions.explanation: The Sahara is defined by extremely low, unreliable rainfall, very sparse vegetation, and large diurnal temperature ranges due to the lack of cloud cover and moisture to moderate heat loss at night.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: The Great Rift Valley, which runs through much of East Africa, is closely associated with which of the following features?
options: Extensive coral reef systems along its full length, with no volcanic activity
A chain of deep lakes and active or dormant volcanoes formed by tensional faulting
A continuous, unbroken mountain range formed entirely by compressional folding
The world's largest hot desert
questions.explanation: The Great Rift Valley formed through tensional faulting associated with the East African Rift system, and is notably associated with a chain of deep rift lakes (such as Lake Tanganyika) and volcanic features (such as Mount Kilimanjaro nearby).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: The River Nile, the longest river in Africa, is formed by the confluence of two major tributaries, namely the
options: Niger and Benue
Congo and Zambezi
White Nile and Blue Nile
Orange and Limpopo
questions.explanation: The Nile is formed from the union of the White Nile, originating in the Great Lakes region of East Africa, and the Blue Nile, originating in the Ethiopian Highlands, which meet at Khartoum in Sudan.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: The Congo Basin in Central Africa is notable for containing
options: the source of the River Nile
the largest hot desert in the world
Africa's most extensive area of Mediterranean climate
the world's second-largest expanse of tropical rainforest, drained by the Congo River
questions.explanation: The Congo Basin, drained by the Congo River, contains the second-largest continuous tropical rainforest in the world (after the Amazon), supporting immense biodiversity.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: The Sahel region, a semi-arid transitional zone lying just south of the Sahara, is particularly vulnerable to
options: desertification, driven by a combination of low, unreliable rainfall, overgrazing, and unsustainable land use
excessive rainfall and permanent waterlogging
volcanic eruptions and frequent earthquakes
permanent glaciation
questions.explanation: The Sahel's marginal, low, and highly variable rainfall, combined with pressures such as overgrazing and overcultivation, makes it especially prone to land degradation and the southward advance of desert-like conditions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: The Atlas Mountains, located in north-western Africa, were primarily formed through
options: volcanic eruptions along a mid-ocean ridge
compressional folding associated with tectonic plate collision
glacial erosion during the last ice age alone
wind erosion of soft sedimentary rock
questions.explanation: The Atlas Mountains are fold mountains formed by compressional forces associated with the collision and convergence of the African and Eurasian tectonic plates.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: Bitumen, a mineral resource found in commercially significant quantities in Nigeria, is chiefly located in which state?
options: Sokoto State
Kano State
Ondo State
Borno State
questions.explanation: Nigeria's major bitumen deposits, among the largest in the world, are located primarily in Ondo State, in south-western Nigeria.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: Cattle rearing in Nigeria has traditionally been concentrated mainly in the northern part of the country primarily because
options: the north has significantly higher rainfall than the south, favouring pasture growth
the north has no arable farming activity, leaving land exclusively for grazing
cattle cannot survive at all in coastal environments
the savanna vegetation of the north is relatively free of the tsetse fly, whose bite transmits trypanosomiasis (a disease fatal to cattle), unlike the humid south
questions.explanation: The drier savanna environment of northern Nigeria is largely free of the tsetse fly, which thrives in the humid forest zones of the south and transmits trypanosomiasis, a disease that can be fatal to cattle, making northern conditions far more favourable for large-scale cattle rearing.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: Lake Victoria, one of the African Great Lakes and a source region for the White Nile, is bordered by which three countries?
options: Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania
Egypt, Sudan, and Ethiopia
Nigeria, Niger, and Chad
Morocco, Algeria, and Libya
questions.explanation: Lake Victoria, the largest lake in Africa and a key source of the White Nile, is bordered by Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: The depletion of the stratospheric ozone layer, which allows more harmful ultraviolet radiation to reach the Earth's surface, has been primarily linked to the release of
options: carbon dioxide from deforestation alone
chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), historically used in refrigerants and aerosol propellants
excess nitrogen from agricultural fertiliser runoff
particulate matter from desert dust storms
questions.explanation: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), once widely used in refrigeration, air conditioning, and aerosol sprays, release chlorine atoms in the stratosphere that catalytically break down ozone molecules, thinning the protective ozone layer.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: Acid rain is primarily formed when
options: ocean salt is lifted into the atmosphere by strong winds
carbon dioxide alone dissolves in rainwater at completely natural background levels
sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides, released mainly from burning fossil fuels, react with water vapour in the atmosphere to form sulphuric and nitric acids
volcanic ash blocks sunlight from reaching the Earth's surface
questions.explanation: Acid rain forms mainly when sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides, largely released by burning fossil fuels, react with atmospheric water vapour and oxygen to produce sulphuric and nitric acids, which then fall as precipitation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: Which of the following soil conservation methods is specifically designed to reduce soil erosion on sloped agricultural land by ploughing along the natural contours of the slope rather than up and down it?
options: Slash-and-burn clearing
Monoculture
Overgrazing
Contour ploughing
questions.explanation: Contour ploughing involves cultivating along the natural contour lines of a slope rather than up and down it, which slows the downhill flow of surface water and significantly reduces soil erosion.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: Which of the following best distinguishes gully erosion from sheet erosion?
options: Sheet erosion removes a thin, fairly uniform layer of topsoil across a wide area, while gully erosion cuts deep, narrow channels into the land as concentrated water flow increases in volume and speed
Gully erosion removes a thin, uniform layer of topsoil, while sheet erosion cuts deep channels into the land
Sheet erosion occurs only in deserts, while gully erosion occurs only in rainforests
There is no meaningful difference between sheet erosion and gully erosion
questions.explanation: Sheet erosion strips away a thin, relatively even layer of topsoil across a broad area, whereas gully erosion occurs when concentrated surface runoff cuts progressively deeper and wider channels into the land.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: Soil salinization, a significant land degradation hazard in some irrigated agricultural areas, occurs mainly when
options: heavy rainfall washes all soluble salts completely out of the soil
excessive irrigation water evaporates, leaving behind a build-up of dissolved salts in the topsoil
farmers plant only salt-tolerant crops exclusively
volcanic ash deposits accumulate on agricultural land
questions.explanation: In poorly drained irrigated areas, water applied to fields evaporates while dissolved mineral salts remain and accumulate in the topsoil over time, gradually reducing soil fertility and crop productivity.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: Oil spillage in the Niger Delta region of Nigeria has had a particularly severe environmental impact mainly because it
options: improves the fertility of farmland in affected areas
has no lasting effect on the ecosystem, since oil evaporates immediately
contaminates soil, rivers, and mangrove ecosystems, destroying fish habitats and agricultural land relied upon by local communities
only affects areas located far from any human settlement
questions.explanation: Oil spillage in the Niger Delta contaminates soil and waterways, damages sensitive mangrove ecosystems, and destroys the fish stocks and farmland that many local communities depend on for their livelihoods.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: Remote sensing, an important data source for Geographic Information Systems (GIS), is best described as the
options: direct physical measurement of an object obtained by touching or sampling it
storage of geographic data exclusively on paper records
manual drawing of a map using a compass and ruler alone
acquisition of information about the Earth's surface from a distance, typically using sensors mounted on satellites or aircraft
questions.explanation: Remote sensing involves collecting data about the Earth's surface without direct physical contact, typically using sensors carried on satellites or aircraft, making it a key data source for GIS.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: The Global Positioning System (GPS), often used alongside GIS, primarily functions by
options: using a network of satellites to determine the precise geographic location (coordinates) of a receiver on or near the Earth's surface
physically surveying land boundaries using a measuring tape
converting paper maps into digital images through scanning
recording historical population census data
questions.explanation: GPS uses signals from a constellation of orbiting satellites to calculate the precise geographic coordinates of a receiver, providing accurate location data that can be directly integrated into a GIS.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: The essential components of a functioning Geographic Information System (GIS) typically include
options: hardware and software only, with no requirement for data or trained personnel
hardware, software, geographic data, skilled personnel, and defined methods/procedures
only paper maps and a compass
satellite imagery alone, with no computer hardware required
questions.explanation: A complete GIS requires not just computer hardware and software, but also accurate geographic data, trained personnel to manage and interpret it, and established methods and procedures for its effective use.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: A local government planning agency uses GIS to overlay layers of flood-prone areas, population density, and existing infrastructure to decide where to site new drainage channels. This use of GIS primarily demonstrates its application in
options: historical map preservation only, with no analytical purpose
the classification of igneous rock types
disaster risk management and development planning, through the integrated analysis of multiple spatial data layers
the calculation of back bearings between two points
questions.explanation: By overlaying and analysing multiple spatial data layers together, GIS enables planners to identify risk areas and make informed decisions for infrastructure and disaster risk management, a core practical application of the technology.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: The Beaufort scale, used in weather observation, primarily estimates
options: atmospheric pressure from mercury column height
relative humidity using wet and dry bulb thermometers
rainfall intensity using a graduated cylinder
wind speed/force based on observed effects on land or sea surfaces
questions.explanation: The Beaufort scale estimates wind force by relating observed effects, such as the movement of smoke, trees, or sea waves, to a numbered scale of wind speed, without requiring direct instrumental measurement.
